intent: Prove and close log-file symlink escapes for GET and DELETE without blocking regular logs, and verify mapped-private URL refusal at the actual fetch boundary.

reasons.evidence: The log route's refusal behaviour changes for symlinked files; its public GET and DELETE response must be verified.
The completed batch pushes dev and observes hosted CI; the listener proof binds only to loopback.

invariants: GET cannot read and named or bulk DELETE cannot truncate a sentinel outside the authorised log root through an in-root x.log symlink.
Regular in-root logs remain listed, readable and clearable, including Windows development; symlink refusal must not become a server error or expose sentinel contents.
Mapped-private URL addresses are refused before the fetcher reaches a bounded local listener; a direct connection control proves the listener is reachable.
A URL-guard candidate already covered by existing tests is recorded as a confirmed boundary or refuted defect, not changed for line-count appearance.
rollback: Revert the log handling only with a replacement realpath or descriptor-based containment guard that passes the same isolated sentinel oracle. Retain URL proof independently if no URL source change is needed.
verify_line: On Linux an isolated in-root x.log symlink to an outside sentinel is refused by both GET and DELETE without changing sentinel hash; regular logs still work, mapped private URL addresses are refused in a bounded listener probe, and the Windows-focused guard suite passes.
oracle_provenance: Red-first commit 4e40ef4c introduced six real-filesystem and listener cases. Windows Jest was red at one failure, four Linux-only skips and one pass; test TypeScript passed. A disposable node:24 Linux clone of that committed oracle failed four of six cases against unmodified source. Independent amendment 7652d393 added seven hardlink and dangling-link cases, red at five of seven on Windows. The combined committed Linux oracle failed ten of thirteen, then passed thirteen of thirteen after only the two working source files were copied. The same listener case passed on both sides, refuting the proposed mapped-private URL source defect. The original five-case filesystem oracle later received a fixture-order-only amendment by a different author: all five test names and fourteen assertions stayed identical while the cross-file repeated-window count fell from 4,802 to 4,786. The listener and seven-case alias oracles remained frozen.
approval: The operator approved the complete Phase 2 plan on 2026-09-28 and authorised prerelease T-0180–T-0187. Q-011 still gates structural work on the operator's rc.1 and v1.0.0 release.
review: Independent R2 reviewer Pauli confirmed planted leaf-symlink protection but found hardlink and dangling-link gaps in the first implementation. A separate seven-case red-first amendment proved them. The final read-only review found no planted static leaf-alias bypass and narrowed one proposed mutant's claim to response-contract evidence; it explicitly did not claim atomic protection from a continuously mutating local adversary.
verification: Implementation e116f5fc passed the exact primary-tree ten-step gate by exit code with no tree movement, SHA-256 86aa0180d1ce00268cdd91e8b460814f2d262854a77f3437b9d19c664a72c75c: lint, TypeScript, 758 passing Jest suites (7,344 tests passed, eight skipped), Knip, canary, production build, build purity, 316 Playwright passes (24 skipped) on port 3000, design and line censuses. An isolated managed checkout independently passed all ten steps with SHA-256 d2aefab9e1fa7cb8475611b466077a45c6b04339e0e3831a8bdf292eb7f44dae. Both runs used separate PS_DATA_DIR and HERMES_HOME; 97 tracked files had checkout-specific line endings, so the primary gate established byte identity for the committed tree. The committed native-Linux real-filesystem oracle passed all 13 cases; Windows focused checks passed 40 cases with four Linux-only skips. Exact-head push CI 36467397118, PR CI 36467405410, push Gitleaks 36467397002 and PR Gitleaks 36467405370 all concluded successfully. Every PR CI job passed, including full browser acceptance, real Hermes, install/update, Docker, Ubuntu and macOS. Push CI skipped its full E2E job by existing event condition.
mutation: A disposable native-Linux clone of clean e116f5fc passed unmodified controls, killed all three T-0181 mutants through structured Jest assertion failures, restored source in finally and passed the final control. No mutant was NOT-APPLIED, INEFFECTIVE or SURVIVED. Windows refused the control because platform-specific tests are skipped there; it was not reported as a kill.
deviation: Two full-gate attempts stopped honestly before the final green run: a stale derived task view, then a genuine test repeated-window ceiling of 4,802 against 4,800. The view was rendered from the canonical record and a different-author fixture reorder reduced the window count to 4,786 without moving the ceiling. The primary gate first stopped on an old ignored .gate visual helper with forbidden CommonJS imports; it was preserved outside the repository and the entire gate reran. The first isolated worktree had different checkout line endings, so the exact primary-tree gate was also run. No source change was made to the already-correct mapped-private URL guard. Concurrent agent assignments had disjoint task-record claims and on-disk briefs, but org/claims.json was not populated during the overlap; the next concurrent-writing batch must establish live claims before dispatch.
